source_spans.quote: (1) Definitions In this chapter:

claim_judgments.rationale: Claim C0000 accurately sets out the statutory definition of 'individualized education program' (IEP) in 20 U.S.C. 1414(d)(1)(A), faithfully incorporating all statutory components (I) through (VIII) including present levels, measurable annual goals, progress reporting, special education and related services, extent of nonparticipation with nondisabled peers, testing accommodations/alternate assessments, service commencement details, and transition requirements.

source_spans.quote:
(ii) Rule of construction Nothing in this section shall be construed to require—

(I) that additional information be included in a child’s IEP beyond what is explicitly required in this section; and

claim_judgments.rationale: Claim C0001 captures the rule of construction in 20 U.S.C. 1414(d)(1)(A)(ii)(I) providing that nothing in the section shall be construed to require additional information beyond what is explicitly required in the section.

source_spans.quote: (ii) Rule of construction Nothing in this section shall be construed to require—
(II) the IEP Team to include information under 1 component of a child’s IEP that is already contained under another component of such IEP.

claim_judgments.rationale: Claim C0002 accurately articulates the rule of construction in 20 U.S.C. 1414(d)(1)(A)(ii)(II) that the IEP Team is not required to include information under one component of an IEP that is already contained under another component.

source_spans.quote: (1) Definitions In this chapter:

claim_judgments.rationale: Claim C0003 correctly defines 'individualized education program team' or 'IEP Team' pursuant to 20 U.S.C. 1414(d)(1)(B), detailing each required and permissive member across clauses (i) through (vii).

source_spans.quote: A member of the IEP Team shall not be required to attend an IEP meeting, in whole or in part, if the parent of a child with a disability and the local educational agency agree that the attendance of such member is not necessary because the member’s area of the curriculum or related services is not being modified or discussed in the meeting.

claim_judgments.rationale: Claim C0004 faithfully reflects 20 U.S.C. 1414(d)(1)(C)(i), exempting an IEP Team member from meeting attendance when the parent and agency agree the attendance is not necessary because the member's area is not modified or discussed.

source_spans.quote:
(ii) Excusal A member of the IEP Team may be excused from attending an IEP meeting, in whole or in part, when the meeting involves a modification to or discussion of the member’s area of the curriculum or related services, if—

(I) the parent and the local educational agency consent to the excusal; and

(II) the member submits, in writing to the parent and the IEP Team, input into the development of the IEP prior to the meeting.

claim_judgments.rationale: Claim C0005 accurately represents 20 U.S.C. 1414(d)(1)(C)(ii), covering permissive excusal of an IEP Team member when their area is modified or discussed, subject to written input and parent/agency consent.

source_spans.quote: A parent’s agreement under clause (i) and consent under clause (ii) shall be in writing.

claim_judgments.rationale: Claim C0006 accurately states the statutory requirement under 20 U.S.C. 1414(d)(1)(C)(iii) that a parent's agreement under clause (i) and consent under clause (ii) must be in writing.

source_spans.quote: In the case of a child who was previously served under subchapter III, an invitation to the initial IEP meeting shall, at the request of the parent, be sent to the subchapter III service coordinator or other representatives of the subchapter III system to assist with the smooth transition of services.

claim_judgments.rationale: Claim C0007 correctly sets forth 20 U.S.C. 1414(d)(1)(D), requiring an invitation to the initial IEP meeting to be sent to the subchapter III service coordinator/representative upon parental request.

source_spans.quote: (1) Definitions In this chapter:

(i) In general The term “individualized education program” or “IEP” means a written statement for each child with a disability that is developed, reviewed, and revised in accordance with this section and that includes—

unit_judgments.rationale: Covered by claim C0000, which includes the definition of individualized education program or IEP under 20 U.S.C. 1414(d)(1)(A).

source_spans.quote: (I) a statement of the child’s present levels of academic achievement and functional performance, including—

unit_judgments.rationale: Covered in claim C0000's summary describing present levels of academic achievement and functional performance under subclause (I).

source_spans.quote: (aa) how the child’s disability affects the child’s involvement and progress in the general education curriculum;

unit_judgments.rationale: Covered in claim C0000's summary detailing how disability affects involvement and progress in the general education curriculum under item (aa).

source_spans.quote: (bb) for preschool children, as appropriate, how the disability affects the child’s participation in appropriate activities; and

unit_judgments.rationale: Covered in claim C0000's summary concerning preschool participation in appropriate activities under item (bb).

source_spans.quote: (cc) for children with disabilities who take alternate assessments aligned to alternate achievement standards, a description of benchmarks or short-term objectives;

unit_judgments.rationale: Covered in claim C0000's summary detailing benchmarks or short-term objectives for children taking alternate assessments aligned to alternate achievement standards under item (cc).

source_spans.quote: (II) a statement of measurable annual goals, including academic and functional goals, designed to—

unit_judgments.rationale: Covered in claim C0000's summary setting out measurable annual goals including academic and functional goals under subclause (II).

source_spans.quote: (aa) meet the child’s needs that result from the child’s disability to enable the child to be involved in and make progress in the general education curriculum; and

unit_judgments.rationale: Covered in claim C0000's summary detailing annual goals designed to enable general education curriculum involvement and progress under item (aa).

source_spans.quote: (bb) meet each of the child’s other educational needs that result from the child’s disability;

unit_judgments.rationale: Covered in claim C0000's summary addressing goals meeting each other educational need resulting from the disability under item (bb).

source_spans.quote: (III) a description of how the child’s progress toward meeting the annual goals described in subclause (II) will be measured and when periodic reports on the progress the child is making toward meeting the annual goals (such as through the use of quarterly or other periodic reports, concurrent with the issuance of report cards) will be provided;

unit_judgments.rationale: Covered in claim C0000's summary setting out the description of progress measurement and timing of periodic progress reports under subclause (III).

source_spans.quote: (IV) a statement of the special education and related services and supplementary aids and services, based on peer-reviewed research to the extent practicable, to be provided to the child, or on behalf of the child, and a statement of the program modifications or supports for school personnel that will be provided for the child—

unit_judgments.rationale: Covered in claim C0000's summary stating special education, related services, supplementary aids, and personnel modifications/supports under subclause (IV).

source_spans.quote: (aa) to advance appropriately toward attaining the annual goals;

unit_judgments.rationale: Covered in claim C0000's summary addressing advancement toward attaining annual goals under item (aa).

source_spans.quote: (bb) to be involved in and make progress in the general education curriculum in accordance with subclause (I) and to participate in extracurricular and other nonacademic activities; and

unit_judgments.rationale: Covered in claim C0000's summary addressing involvement in general curriculum and participation in extracurricular/nonacademic activities under item (bb).

source_spans.quote: (cc) to be educated and participate with other children with disabilities and nondisabled children in the activities described in this subparagraph;

unit_judgments.rationale: Covered in claim C0000's summary covering participation and education with nondisabled children under item (cc).

source_spans.quote: (V) an explanation of the extent, if any, to which the child will not participate with nondisabled children in the regular class and in the activities described in subclause (IV)(cc);

unit_judgments.rationale: Covered in claim C0000's summary setting out the explanation of nonparticipation with nondisabled children under subclause (V).

source_spans.quote:
(VI)

(aa) a statement of any individual appropriate accommodations that are necessary to measure the academic achievement and functional performance of the child on State and districtwide assessments consistent with section 1412(a)(16)(A) of this title; and

unit_judgments.rationale: Covered in claim C0000's summary detailing assessment accommodations consistent with section 1412(a)(16)(A) under subclause (VI)(aa).

source_spans.quote: (bb) if the IEP Team determines that the child shall take an alternate assessment on a particular State or districtwide assessment of student achievement, a statement of why—

unit_judgments.rationale: Covered in claim C0000's summary detailing the alternate assessment condition and requirements under subclause (VI)(bb).

source_spans.quote: (AA) the child cannot participate in the regular assessment; and

unit_judgments.rationale: Covered in claim C0000's summary explaining why the child cannot participate in the regular assessment under subclause (VI)(bb)(AA).

source_spans.quote: (BB) the particular alternate assessment selected is appropriate for the child;

unit_judgments.rationale: Covered in claim C0000's summary explaining why the alternate assessment selected is appropriate under subclause (VI)(bb)(BB).

source_spans.quote: (VII) the projected date for the beginning of the services and modifications described in subclause (IV), and the anticipated frequency, location, and duration of those services and modifications; and

unit_judgments.rationale: Covered in claim C0000's summary stating projected start date, frequency, location, and duration of services under subclause (VII).

source_spans.quote: (VIII) beginning not later than the first IEP to be in effect when the child is 16, and updated annually thereafter—

unit_judgments.rationale: Covered in claim C0000's summary regarding the timing of transition goals (first IEP in effect when child is 16 and updated annually) under subclause (VIII).

source_spans.quote: (aa) appropriate measurable postsecondary goals based upon age appropriate transition assessments related to training, education, employment, and, where appropriate, independent living skills;

unit_judgments.rationale: Covered in claim C0000's summary regarding postsecondary goals based on transition assessments under item (aa).

source_spans.quote: (bb) the transition services (including courses of study) needed to assist the child in reaching those goals; and

unit_judgments.rationale: Covered in claim C0000's summary regarding transition services needed to assist in reaching goals under item (bb).

source_spans.quote: (cc) beginning not later than 1 year before the child reaches the age of majority under State law, a statement that the child has been informed of the child’s rights under this chapter, if any, that will transfer to the child on reaching the age of majority under section 1415(m) of this title.

unit_judgments.rationale: Covered in claim C0000's summary regarding transfer of rights notification 1 year before age of majority under item (cc).

source_spans.quote: (ii) Rule of construction Nothing in this section shall be construed to require—

unit_judgments.rationale: Jointly covered by claims C0001 and C0002, which cover the lead-in and respective branches of the rule of construction in 20 U.S.C. 1414(d)(1)(A)(ii).

source_spans.quote:
(ii) Rule of construction Nothing in this section shall be construed to require—

(I) that additional information be included in a child’s IEP beyond what is explicitly required in this section; and

unit_judgments.rationale: Covered by claim C0001, which sets out the rule of construction in subclause (I) regarding additional information not explicitly required.

source_spans.quote: (ii) Rule of construction Nothing in this section shall be construed to require—
(II) the IEP Team to include information under 1 component of a child’s IEP that is already contained under another component of such IEP.

unit_judgments.rationale: Covered by claim C0002, which sets out the rule of construction in subclause (II) regarding duplicate components.

source_spans.quote: (1) Definitions In this chapter:
(B) Individualized education program team The term “individualized education program team” or “IEP Team” means a group of individuals composed of—

unit_judgments.rationale: Covered by claim C0003, which defines the IEP Team under 20 U.S.C. 1414(d)(1)(B).

source_spans.quote: (i) the parents of a child with a disability;

unit_judgments.rationale: Covered in claim C0003's summary specifying the inclusion of parents under clause (i).

source_spans.quote: (ii) not less than 1 regular education teacher of such child (if the child is, or may be, participating in the regular education environment);

unit_judgments.rationale: Covered in claim C0003's summary specifying not less than 1 regular education teacher under clause (ii).

source_spans.quote: (iii) not less than 1 special education teacher, or where appropriate, not less than 1 special education provider of such child;

unit_judgments.rationale: Covered in claim C0003's summary specifying not less than 1 special education teacher/provider under clause (iii).

source_spans.quote: (iv) a representative of the local educational agency who—

unit_judgments.rationale: Covered in claim C0003's summary specifying the representative of the local educational agency under clause (iv).

source_spans.quote: (I) is qualified to provide, or supervise the provision of, specially designed instruction to meet the unique needs of children with disabilities;

unit_judgments.rationale: Covered in claim C0003's summary specifying the LEA representative's qualification to provide/supervise specially designed instruction under subclause (I).

source_spans.quote: (II) is knowledgeable about the general education curriculum; and

unit_judgments.rationale: Covered in claim C0003's summary specifying the LEA representative's knowledge of the general curriculum under subclause (II).

source_spans.quote: (III) is knowledgeable about the availability of resources of the local educational agency;

unit_judgments.rationale: Covered in claim C0003's summary specifying the LEA representative's knowledge of LEA resources under subclause (III).

source_spans.quote: (v) an individual who can interpret the instructional implications of evaluation results, who may be a member of the team described in clauses (ii) through (vi);

unit_judgments.rationale: Covered in claim C0003's summary specifying the individual who can interpret instructional implications under clause (v).

source_spans.quote: (vi) at the discretion of the parent or the agency, other individuals who have knowledge or special expertise regarding the child, including related services personnel as appropriate; and

unit_judgments.rationale: Covered in claim C0003's summary specifying discretionary members with knowledge or special expertise under clause (vi).

source_spans.quote: (vii) whenever appropriate, the child with a disability.

unit_judgments.rationale: Covered in claim C0003's summary specifying the child with a disability whenever appropriate under clause (vii).

source_spans.quote: A member of the IEP Team shall not be required to attend an IEP meeting, in whole or in part, if the parent of a child with a disability and the local educational agency agree that the attendance of such member is not necessary because the member’s area of the curriculum or related services is not being modified or discussed in the meeting.

unit_judgments.rationale: Covered by claim C0004, which sets out the attendance exemption when the member's area is not modified or discussed under 20 U.S.C. 1414(d)(1)(C)(i).

source_spans.quote: (ii) Excusal A member of the IEP Team may be excused from attending an IEP meeting, in whole or in part, when the meeting involves a modification to or discussion of the member’s area of the curriculum or related services, if—

unit_judgments.rationale: Covered by claim C0005, which sets out the excusal provision under 20 U.S.C. 1414(d)(1)(C)(ii).

source_spans.quote: (I) the parent and the local educational agency consent to the excusal; and

unit_judgments.rationale: Covered in claim C0005's summary specifying parent and LEA consent to excusal under subclause (I).

source_spans.quote: (II) the member submits, in writing to the parent and the IEP Team, input into the development of the IEP prior to the meeting.

unit_judgments.rationale: Covered in claim C0005's summary specifying written input prior to the meeting under subclause (II).

source_spans.quote: A parent’s agreement under clause (i) and consent under clause (ii) shall be in writing.

unit_judgments.rationale: Covered by claim C0006, which provides that agreement under clause (i) and consent under clause (ii) must be in writing under 20 U.S.C. 1414(d)(1)(C)(iii).

source_spans.quote: In the case of a child who was previously served under subchapter III, an invitation to the initial IEP meeting shall, at the request of the parent, be sent to the subchapter III service coordinator or other representatives of the subchapter III system to assist with the smooth transition of services.

unit_judgments.rationale: Covered by claim C0007, which details the transition invitation to subchapter III representatives under 20 U.S.C. 1414(d)(1)(D).
